- bash (intenção: Re-verifying three chapters after format correction | comando: cd /home/one/projects/one/ai-guides/runtimes/docker_engine_guide && python3 - <<'PY'
import re, pathlib
P=pathlib.Path('/tmp/docker-research/pages'); G=pathlib.Path('.')
files=['12-runtime-flags.md','21-determinism-deep.md','22-security-hardening-deep.md']
TOK=re.compile(r'`((?:pages|samples)/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*\.md):(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?`')
BARE=re.compile(r'(?<![`\w])pages/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.md:\d+')
PT=re.compile(r'\b(não|verificado|configuração|segurança|imagens|execução|padrão|comando|documentação|limites|visão|ferramentas)\b',re.I)
exp={'12':'runtime-flags','21':'determinism-deep','22':'security-hardening-deep'}
for f in files:
    raw=pathlib.Path(f).read_bytes(); text=raw.decode(); lines=text.splitlines()
    toks=TOK.findall(text); bad=[]
    for t,a,b in toks:
        p=P/t[len('pages/'):] if t.startswith('pages/') else G/t
        if not p.is_file(): bad.append('missing '+t); continue
        n=len(p.read_text().splitlines()); a=int(a); b=int(b or a)
        if not (1<=a<=b<=n): bad.append(f'range {t}:{a}-{b}/{n}')
    tail=text.rsplit('## Sources',1)[-1]; urls=re.findall(r'https://\S+',tail)
    fences=[l for l in lines if l.startswith('```')]
    print(f'{f}: {len(raw)}B inband={6000<=len(raw)<=9000} heading_ok={lines[0]=="# "+f[:2]+" - "+exp[f[:2]]} cites={len(toks)} bad={bad} bare={len(BARE.findall(text))} urls={len(urls)} official={all(u.startswith("https://docs.docker.com/") for u in urls)} pt={bool(PT.search(text))} fences={len(fences)}')
PY)

01-engine-architecture.md:7:The daemon does not create containers itself. It delegates lifecycle work to containerd, which by default invokes runc as the OCI runtime. Alternative runtimes plug in through containerd shims. pages/engine/daemon/alternative-runtimes.md:4-13
01-engine-architecture.md:12:| `dockerd` | Owns the API, images, networks, volumes; starts/manages containerd | pages/engine/daemon/start.md:27-34, pages/engine/daemon/embedded-containerd.md:4-6 |

01-engine-architecture.md:15:| containerd shim | One per task; kept as a separate process even in embedded mode | pages/engine/daemon/embedded-containerd.md:13-16, pages/engine/daemon/alternative-runtimes.md:10-13 |
01-engine-architecture.md:17:Since Engine 29.7.0 an experimental `embedded-containerd` feature runs containerd inside the `dockerd` process, reaching it over an in-memory connection while task shims stay separate. It is mutually exclusive with `cri-containerd`, keeps state under `/var/lib/docker/containerd/daemon`, and is enabled with `"features": {"embedded-containerd": true}` or `--feature embedded-containerd`. pages/engine/daemon/embedded-containerd.md:4-6,13-28,54-66 Docker stores containers in the `moby` containerd namespace by default. pages/engine/daemon/embedded-containerd.md:95-96
01-engine-architecture.md:21:By default the daemon listens on a Unix socket at `/var/run/docker.sock`, requiring `root` or `docker` group membership. It can also listen via `tcp` and `fd` sockets; TCP gives unencrypted, unauthenticated access unless TLS or a proxy secures it, and port `2375` is conventional for plain traffic, `2376` for TLS. pages/reference/cli/dockerd.md:178-193
01-engine-architecture.md:24:pages/engine/daemon/start.md:36-42
01-engine-architecture.md:33:Remote access may be set through a systemd unit or `daemon.json`, but not both: configuring both causes a conflict that prevents Docker from starting. pages/engine/daemon/remote-access.md:22-28,66-69 The API surface is versioned; the captured history reaches v1.56, which adds an `annotation` filter on `GET /containers/json` and `HostConfig.Umask` on `POST /containers/create`. pages/reference/api/engine/version-history.md:11-21
01-engine-architecture.md:35:A systemd drop-in is the documented way to add a listener without touching `daemon.json` (where the `-H` flag already set by Debian/Ubuntu units would conflict). pages/engine/daemon/troubleshoot.md:94-99
01-engine-architecture.md:36:pages/engine/daemon/remote-access.md:37-41
01-engine-architecture.md:42:Verify with `netstat -lntp | grep dockerd`; the documented default TLS port is `2376`, plain `2375`. pages/engine/daemon/remote-access.md:57-62,89-94
01-engine-architecture.md:46:Installation methods are: bundled in Docker Desktop, the distribution `apt` repository, manual `.deb` packages (manage upgrades yourself), or a convenience script recommended only for testing and development. pages/engine/install/ubuntu.md:80-94 Setting up the repository once allows later install and update from it. pages/engine/install/ubuntu.md:103-107 Upgrade is "follow step 2 of the installation instructions, choosing the new version"; the package path requires downloading a new `.deb` on each upgrade. pages/engine/install/ubuntu.md:207-217
01-engine-architecture.md:49:pages/engine/install/ubuntu.md:148-163
01-engine-architecture.md:57:On a typical install a system utility, not a user, starts the daemon so it restarts on reboot. pages/engine/daemon/start.md:4-10 On Ubuntu/Debian it starts automatically; to start manually use `sudo systemctl start docker` (`Ctrl+C` stops a foreground `dockerd`). pages/engine/daemon/start.md:15-25,44-45 For systemd hosts without default boot start: pages/engine/install/linux-postinstall.md:221-239
01-engine-architecture.md:62:Use `disable` instead to stop that behavior; unit files can add proxies or alternate runtime directories. pages/engine/install/linux-postinstall.md:234-244
01-engine-architecture.md:66:A feature is labeled "deprecated" and remains for at least one stable release before removal, so operators must track each release's deprecation list. pages/engine/deprecated.md:18-28 The current line is Engine 28.x and 29.x: 28.5.2 shipped runc CVE fixes, while 29.10.0 is the newest 29.x entry in the captured notes. pages/engine/release-notes/28.md:11-25, pages/engine/release-notes/29.md:11
01-engine-architecture.md:68:Daemon logs live in OS-specific locations — on Linux use `journalctl -xu docker.service` or `/var/log/syslog`/`/var/log/messages`. pages/engine/daemon/logs.md:4-13 For structured daemon logs set `"log-format": "json"` (default `text`); do not set both the flag and the file key. pages/reference/cli/dockerd.md:916-941 Enable debug via `"debug": true` and `SIGHUP`; force a stack trace with `SIGUSR1` without stopping the daemon. pages/engine/daemon/logs.md:35-39,59-64,73-76 `docker info` reports system-wide state including kernel version and container/image counts. pages/reference/cli/docker/system/info.md:16-24
02-daemon-configuration.md:7:Default Linux path is `/etc/docker/daemon.json` (Windows: `%programdata%\docker\config\daemon.json`); `--config-file` overrides it. pages/reference/cli/dockerd.md:1085-1089,1237-1242 Keys mirror flag names, pluralized for repeatable flags (`labels` for `--label`). pages/reference/cli/dockerd.md:1054-1057 Duplicating a key as a flag fails startup regardless of value; a systemd `-H` colliding with `hosts` is the common case. pages/reference/cli/dockerd.md:1059-1065, pages/engine/daemon/troubleshoot.md:66-99 Direct daemon configuration outranks proxy environment variables. pages/engine/daemon/proxy.md:20-31
